findings.reason: a judged-count cap needs either a cursor/offset that advances past withheld rows or an ordering that judges prune candidates first; without one the node ships a bound that livelocks and reports success, and the fix must be specified before dispatch rather than discovered by the worker.
findings.text: the deliverable's fix, "--limit counts every judged directory, not only offered ones", is applied to a loop that iterates `sorted(path for path in runs_root.iterdir() if path.is_dir())` from the first entry on every pass (`reckon/crew/gc.py:1533`) and breaks once the cap is reached (gc.py:1562); with the cap moved onto judged rows, two withheld classes that never clear — `review-owed` (gc.py:306-324) and `missing-derived-figure` (gc.py:337-353) — sit at the head of that order, so a prefix of `limit` such rows makes every pass judge the same prefix, remove nothing, and never reach the runs behind it. §1 records 8,861 review runs of 17,341, so this is not a corner case, and it contradicts §7's landed claim that "the first passes reclaim the existing backlog at that rate" (plan.html:183) as well as this section's own Why, "the reaper §7 installs would then reap nothing".

findings.reason: the done-when's host measure needs a path §3 does not retire — a committed evidence fragment under `docs/evidence/fragments/crew-state-stays-bounded/` or a gate log — otherwise the plan's one measurement of real-store cost cannot be checked, which is the exact defect §10 exists to end.
findings.text: "its per-phase timings are cited in the manifest" names the run manifest as the durable record of the only host measurement the done-when rests on, but §3 states "The run's durable facts are its ledger row, its committed run record and its evidence fragment" (plan.html:118) and retires a finished run's directory after a one-day grace (§3, plan.html:117), so the manifest the timings are written to is gone within a day of the run ending and no later reader can open the measure; §5 and §8's sections both required a committed evidence fragment and gate log for this reason.

findings.reason: the attribution is the input that decides which phase the bound must actually target; leaving it unmeasured lets a node satisfy the gate while bounding the wrong phase, and it is one clause to add.
findings.text: the Deliverable requires the node to "First measure the pass on a quiet window, with per-phase timings, and name the slow phase", but the Done when lists only the new test's two cases, the host wall-clock bound and the suite/ruff clauses; nothing in the gate reddens when the slow phase is unnamed or when the measurement was taken on a loaded node, even though the Why itself says "That run shared the node with parallel censuses and a 1.65 TB copy, so the cost is not yet attributed".
